qualitative.gate_2_reason: Commodity price taker lacking pricing power in cyclical upstream natural gas exploration & production.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 2 (Rejected – G2 Essential Need). Pure-play upstream natural gas exploration and production company selling an undifferentiated commodity into cyclical spot markets with zero structural pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Formed via the October 2024 merger of Chesapeake Energy and Southwestern Energy, Expand Energy is the largest US natural gas producer, operating across the Haynesville and Marcellus shale basins. Despite substantial production scale (~7.5 Bcfe/d) and post-merger cost synergies, the company operates as an upstream commodity price-taker whose margins and cash flows fluctuate with spot natural gas prices. Capital efficiency is structurally sub-hurdle (10-year median ROIC ~7.2% vs. 12% compounder threshold), and predecessor Chesapeake underwent Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2020 due to severe commodity price declines and debt overhang.
